sections.html:
Kingman is the Mohave County seat, which helps a seller: the recorder, assessor, treasurer and courts are all downtown, a short walk apart. Fast sales here usually follow one of two paths, an agent listing or a direct deal with a cash buyer, and the legal paperwork is identical in both.

An agent listing opens the house to the most buyers, though it depends on showings, a loan and an appraisal. Cash deals typically skip the loan and the appraisal. That trims the calendar, and in return the offer reflects the repairs and risk the buyer inherits. Before choosing, round up these items:

  • Recorded deed and Mohave County parcel number
  • Payoff statements for a mortgage, home equity line or lien
  • Permit records for any work on the house
  • Contacts for an HOA or special district, if the lot belongs to one
  • Your latest property tax bill

The population is an estimated 35,829 as of July 1, 2025, up 9.6 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners live in 68.4 percent of homes. A median owner-occupied home is worth $267,700, median gross rent is $1,058, median household income is $61,792, and the 15,206 households average 2.20 people. These are rough anchors only, so ask a local agent or appraiser to show you comparable sales near your address.

At about 3,471 feet, Kingman covers roughly 37.5 square miles and sits where Interstate 40 meets U.S. 93. Summer highs rarely pass 107 degrees, but winter nights often fall below freezing, snow can arrive, and rainfall is about 8 inches a year. Inspectors here look hard at the heating system, pipe insulation and roof, not just the air conditioner.

An unpermitted project is the likeliest thing to slow a Kingman sale. Development Services runs a Building Division that handles applications for residential, commercial, industrial, demolition and signage work. Phone (928) 753-8130 about your address before you list. A residential permit process guide explains the Minor Improvement Permit, the route for smaller jobs.

Book inspections by phone, with the request in before 7:00 a.m. on the day you want the inspector and your permit number and job site address on hand. An older patio cover, room addition or garage conversion deserves a call: find out what the city has on file and what a retroactive permit would involve. Sorting that out before offers arrive spares you a renegotiation after the inspection.

A house outside city limits, in unincorporated Mohave County, can fall under A.R.S. 33-422 if the seller offers five or fewer parcels of land, not counting subdivided land. In that case the buyer gets a written affidavit of disclosure at least seven days before transfer, plus a five-day right to rescind.

Under Ordinance No. 1952, effective October 1, 2023, renting a house by the night inside city limits takes a city permit. The permit requires a $60 annual fee, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, a 24-hour emergency contact and written notice to neighboring homes. Skipping the permit can cost up to $1,000 a month in fines. A.R.S. 9-500.39 limits how far a city can restrict such rentals, yet a permit requirement is allowed.

Prospective buyers who plan nightly rentals will ask if your property is permitted. Know the answer, yes or no, before they call.

Two Mohave County Treasurer installments make up the year.

InstallmentDuePast due after
First halfOctober 1November 1, 5:00 p.m.
Second halfMarch 1May 1, 5:00 p.m.

If November 1 lands on a weekend, the cutoff slides to the next business day. Paying a bill over $100 in a single payment by December 31 wipes out interest that built up after November 1. Late balances accrue 16 percent a year, prorated monthly.

At closing, the escrow officer shows how this year's tax is prorated. Should a bill show up after the sale, pass it to the new owner or mail it back to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402, noting that the house sold. The Assessor, at 928-753-0703, can verify that the sale was recorded.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Mohave County
sections.html:
The Mohave County Recorder, 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, records your deed for a listed $30 fee. Arizona law (A.R.S. 11-1133) wants an Affidavit of Property Value attached to any deed that moves title, unless the deed shows an exemption notation. Without one the recorder rejects the deed. Title and escrow companies normally prepare it all, since recorder staff will not guide you through the forms.

The recorder's self-service search turns up recorded liens by name. Even a clean result leaves gaps, so buyers purchase title insurance. A copy of a recorded deed costs $1.00 per page.

Once you pick a buyer, the title company opens an escrow file and runs a lien search under your name. It orders a payoff from your lender, drafts the deed and the affidavit, and works out the tax split. You sign, funds move, and the deed is recorded across town on Beale Street. In a cash purchase the whole sequence can wrap up in a short stretch, because there is no loan committee to satisfy.

Plan the practical side too. Decide when you will be out, whether any furniture or tools stay behind, and who gets the garage remotes. Shut off or transfer utilities on the closing date, and take photos of the empty rooms for your own records.

sections.h2: Who buys Kingman houses that need work
sections.html:
Cash buyers and investors are the natural audience for a house with old repairs, tenants, a murky inherited title or a payment problem. Their offers include the cost of the work and the time it takes. Expect a figure under a fully repaired retail sale, traded for speed and fewer conditions.

Judge each offer by what lands in your pocket. Ask who covers escrow and title charges, how many days the buyer needs, whether the house is accepted as is, and what becomes of the deposit if the buyer walks away. Insist on the offer in writing and read the contract before signing. If your mortgage is behind, request a payoff figure and the sale deadline from the lender first, since that date shapes your choices.

After closing, keep the settlement statement, forward any mail that carries the old address, and confirm with the Assessor that the new owner's name is on the parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Kingman house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, a house can be offered as is. Loan-backed buyers may request repairs after the appraisal or inspection, whereas investors and cash buyers frequently accept the current condition. Open permits and unpermitted additions can still delay closing, so call Development Services at (928) 753-8130 to check your address.

faqs.q: How long does recording a deed take in Mohave County?
faqs.a: Under A.R.S. 11-480 the recorder reviews each document, and once it is complete and the fee is paid, a recording number is assigned. Mailed originals come back in about 4 to 6 weeks, while in-person documents are returned after scanning.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax if I sell in the middle of the year?
faqs.a: Ask your escrow officer how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer. Mohave County bills are due October 1 and March 1, with the first half past due after November 1. The settlement statement should show the split.
Yes, with a permit. The city requires a permit, a Transaction Privilege Tax license, an emergency contact and neighbor notice for rentals under 30 days inside city limits. The annual fee is $60.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a lien or a title question on a Kingman property?
faqs.a: Start with a title company, because the recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or do research for you. The Mohave County Recorder at (928) 753-0701 can show you how to run a basic search by name, and a title company can tell you whether liens or judgments will cut into your proceeds.
